tagline.text: An emerald cold spring at the source of the Bugang River in Pandan, Antique, with river tubing downstream

location.label: Location
location.text: Sitio Malumpati, Barangay Guia, Pandan, Antique

duration.label: Time needed
duration.text: Half a day to a full day

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱300~700 (entrance, tubing and transport, per person)

airport.label: Nearest airport
airport.text: Kalibo International Airport (KLO) or Caticlan Airport (MPH)

children.text: Malumpati Cold Spring is an emerald-colored spring that rises in the upper Bugang River in Pandan, in the province of Antique on northwestern Panay. You can swim, jump from the diving board and tube down the clear river, and many visitors come on a day trip from Boracay.

Malumpati Cold Spring is a spring resort in Sitio Malumpati, Barangay Guia, in the municipality of Pandan, Antique. Its formal name is Malumpati Health Spring and Tourist Resort, and it sits near the headwaters of the Bugang River system. Water seeping out of the mountain forms a deep pool whose clear blue-green color lies somewhere between emerald and turquoise, which is why the place became known through photos first. The spring itself works as the swimming pool, and the river flowing out of it is the tubing course.

What makes this place special is how clean the water is. Thanks to the long-term care of local residents, the Bugang River was reported in 2014 as a Hall of Fame awardee in the government's national contest for the
cleanest inland body of water

, and Wikipedia reports that the Philippine Senate passed a resolution that year commending Pandan's conservation efforts. Malumpati lies in the upper part of the river, so it is often introduced as the starting point of the cleanest river in the country. Locals believe the water is good for the body and so call it a "health spring," but that is a local belief and not a proven health benefit.

The origin of the name is also interesting. According to local tradition, it comes from the phrase "Malumpat ang Ati," meaning "the Ati jump," which was shortened to Malumpati. The explanation is that the Ati, the indigenous people of Panay, used to jump into this spring to bathe and swim. Today there are a diving board and a jumping platform in the trees at the edge of the spring, and many people still jump in, true to the name.

From Boracay, the spring lies along the road that runs south down the Panay mainland. It takes about an hour and a half to two hours by road from the Caticlan jetty and roughly three to five hours from Iloilo City. That is why Boracay visitors come as a day trip, while travelers along the Antique coast or from Iloilo drop in on the way. The site is not large, so half a day is enough even at a relaxed pace, and its charm lies in a natural atmosphere rather than in fancy facilities. Public transport does not go straight to the spring entrance, so plan on taking a tricycle from Pandan town, and think ahead about when you will head back.

Pandan, the gateway to the spring, is a small town in northern Antique. As a coastal town it has plenty of fresh fish and seafood dishes, and buying snacks and water in town shops beforehand makes eating at the spring easier. The tricycle ride along country roads from the town to the spring is an experience in itself.
A walk of about
10–20 minutes

up the trail from the entrance brings you to the pool where the spring rises. The water is so clear that you can see the stones and fish on the bottom, and the deeper parts turn a dark blue-green. Wikipedia gives the depth of the headspring as about
, and one mapping site (Waymarking) says the smaller spring was plumbed to 30 m without finding the bottom. The water is cold, so even on a hot day you cool off quickly once you get in.
Guides carry the large tubes and lend you a life vest and helmet, and you start above the spring and float down the river. The ride lasts about
15 minutes
, and the current is gentle enough for families with children. Guides push you through the shallow spots, and blogs put the fee at around
per person.

There is a diving board at the edge of the spring, and you can watch local guides and teenagers jump from high spots. Even watching is fun. If you want to jump yourself, check the water depth and follow the staff's instructions, and wear a life vest.

Those who are not strong swimmers can use a life vest or a tube. The water is cold and has deep sections, so children must always be watched by an adult. When the water is clear, you can see all the way to the bottom, which is reassuring.
Shaded nipa huts and thatched-roof cottages suit family gatherings and packed lunches. Day-use rates have been reported at around
depending on size. There are many trees around the spring, so the shade is deep even at midday. The longer you stay, the more you will value time spent resting out of the water.

The river is cited as a model of community-run eco-tourism. Upstream you will find signs about the Malumpati Watershed Reforestation Project and a facility of the Pandan Water District. Because tourism here goes hand in hand with conservation, taking your trash with you is basic courtesy.
Some blogs describe guided trekking, a zipline, rappelling and a climbing wall. Availability and prices change from year to year, so check the notice boards on site.
Leave your Boracay hotel, cross to the Caticlan jetty, and around
take a bus or van toward Pandan and San Jose. If you book a private vehicle through a tour company, this leg is replaced by hotel pickup.
Get off in Pandan town and find a tricycle. Blogs put the ride from Pandan town to Malumpati at around
. It is reassuring to agree with the driver on a pickup time for the return.
Pay the entrance fee at the gate and register for tubing. Collect a life vest and helmet at the changing area and put your phone in a waterproof case.
Walk up to the top of the spring with your guide and tube down the river.
Return to the spring to swim and watch or try the diving board. Rest at a cottage with the snacks you brought.
Eat lunch at a nearby restaurant. If you packed a lunch, eat it at a hut.
Take a tricycle out to the main road and catch a bus to Caticlan. The last bus leaves early, so get moving in good time.
Tour-company packages that include lunch and round-trip transport are listed at around
per person (two operators' 2026 rates, varying by group size and inclusions), but going on your own is much cheaper. The trade-off is that you have to manage the timing yourself.

items.title: Route from Iloilo
items.subtitle: Combined with a drive along the Antique coast

children.text: Leave Iloilo City and head north along the Antique coastal road. With a rental car or a local driver you can stop at roadside churches and beaches.
Arrive in Pandan, have lunch and head to Malumpati.
Enjoy swimming and tubing and take a walk around the spring.
Visit Mag-aba beach or Pandan Bay at the lower end of the Bugang River, then return to your hotel.
Fly from Manila to Caticlan Airport (MPH) or Kalibo International Airport (KLO). Caticlan is close to Pandan by road, so it pairs well with a Boracay visit.
You can also fly to Iloilo Airport (ILO) and travel north overland. Check airline notices for flight times and fares.
Buses toward San Jose and Iloilo, such as Ceres buses, pass through Pandan from Caticlan. One blog reports the trip took about
1 hour 30 minutes to 2 hours
Rather than riding to the town terminal, ask to be dropped at the intersection where Pandan's main street meets the road toward Libertad, which can save time.
The trip from Iloilo City to Pandan by road is described as taking about
3 to 5 hours
. Vans take about 3 hours and buses 4 to 5 hours, but check times and fares locally.
Take a tricycle or motorcycle taxi from Pandan town. Blogs put the one-way fare at about
, and since a ride back is not always waiting at the spring entrance, it is best to agree on a time with your driver.
We could not confirm a direct route from Kalibo. Ask at the local terminal.

The best time is the dry season from November to May, when the water stays clear. When it rains heavily the river turns murky and the flow rises, so tubing operations may change. One travel account reports giving up on swimming because the water was cloudy on a day of heavy rain.
Weekends and holidays are crowded with local families and groups. If you can, go on a weekday morning and avoid the strong midday sun.

blocks.label: Season at a glance
rows: The water is at its cleanest and most comfortable
The cold water is welcome, but the flow can drop toward the end of the dry season
The water can turn murky and tubing may be limited, so check the weather

If you plan to explore Antique at a relaxed pace instead of making a day trip, Pandan town is a good base. Stock up on food and drinks in town beforehand, and you can also catch a tricycle to Malumpati from here. Your accommodation staff can usually introduce a trustworthy driver, which takes the worry out of getting back.

There is almost no lodging right next to the spring, so most people visit on a day trip. If you stay overnight, a small place in Pandan town or by the sea is more convenient. The beaches of Pandan Bay connect by the main road, so try to stop by around sunset.

For food, rely on the restaurant near the entrance or on food you bring to the cottage. One travel account describes eating rice, squid and milkfish (bangus) at a cottage. Dining options are limited, so bring plenty of water and snacks.
The trail up to the spring has wet stones and dirt, so sandals with straps are safer than slippery flip-flops.
Tubing runs in turns, so on busy days there is a wait. Register as soon as you arrive and swim while you wait.
Arriving on a weekday morning means fewer people and better photos.
Water shoes protect the soles of your feet and are comfortable on the rocky bottom.
Bring a waterproof case or rent one on site.
Bring a towel, dry clothes and a plastic bag. Wet clothes are awkward to carry on the bus.
Use the storage at the information booth for valuables and do not bring them to the water.
Get permission from the resort management before flying a drone.
The last bus leaves early, so arrange your ride back with your driver in advance.
To keep the water clean, do not use shampoo or soap in the spring, and take your trash with you.
The water is deep and cold. Non-swimmers and children must wear life vests, and after rain the current gets stronger, so ask your guide whether tubing is possible.
Jumping from the diving board or from trees without checking the depth and the rocks on the bottom is dangerous.
Entrance and tubing fees differ between sources and change, so confirm them on site.
We could not confirm the operating hours. It is said to operate in daylight hours, so do not arrive late.
It gets very crowded on weekends and the tubing wait can be long.
Claims about health benefits are only belief. If you are ill, see a doctor.

blocks.title: Lower Bugang River and Mag-aba Beach

children.text: The river that flows from the spring meets the sea at Mag-aba on Pandan Bay. It lies within the same municipality of Pandan, reached by following the river downstream, so check the exact travel time locally.
White-sand beaches run from Mag-aba to Duyong. It is a good place to watch the sunset after tubing.
It is about an hour and a half to two hours overland from the Caticlan jetty, so it is a popular day trip from Boracay.
Heading south along the Antique coast brings you to Iloilo City, about
3 to 5 hours
away.
